questions.question: The first parallel government, following the Quit India Movement, was established in which city?
questions.solution:

__
 
• The **first parallel government** after the **Quit India Movement** was established in **Ballia****,** Maharashtra.
 
• It was known as the **Prati Sarkar**, which translates to "parallel government."
 
• The Prati Sarkar was established in **1943** and lasted until **1946**.
 
• The movement was led by **Y.B. Chavan**, **Nana Patil**, and others who organized local governance systems to resist British authority.
 
• It aimed to provide an **alternate governance model** in areas liberated from British control.
 
• Satara became a center for revolutionary activities, with leaders organizing local administration, justice systems, and economic policies.
 
• The Quit India Movement, launched in **1942**, had widespread impact, but Satara's Prati Sarkar stood out as a unique example of localized governance.
 
• The Prati Sarkar also focused on **social reforms**, such as providing education and addressing grievances of the common people.
 
• This initiative showcased the **strength of grassroots-level movements** in India's struggle for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ballia**__

 __
 
• **Ballia** is a district in **Uttar Pradesh**, which also played a key role during the **Quit India Movement**.
 
• Ballia briefly declared independence from British rule, and leaders like **Chittu Pandey** were associated with this revolutionary activity.
 
• Although revolutionary activities occurred here, it did not establish a formal parallel government.
 
 
 
• **Talcher**__
 __
 
• **Talcher** is located in **Odisha**, known for its coal mines and industrial importance.
 
• While Talcher was part of revolutionary activities during India's independence struggle, it was not associated with the establishment of a parallel government.
 
 
 
• **Benaras**__
 
 
• **Benaras**, now known as **Varanasi**, is a cultural and religious hub in **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It played a significant role in the freedom movement, being a center for nationalist activities and home to leaders like **Madan Mohan Malaviya**.
 
• However, Benaras did not establish a parallel government during the Quit India Movement.

questions.question: The irrigation method in India that distributes water through pipes under low pressure to each plant is called:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Localised Irrigation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Localised Irrigation**, also referred to as **micro-irrigation**, involves delivering water directly to the root zone of plants through a network of pipes under **low pressure**.
 
• This method is highly **efficient** as it reduces water wastage and ensures that plants receive the required amount of water directly at their roots.
 
• It is commonly used in **arid and semi-arid regions** where water scarcity is a significant concern.
 
• There are different forms of localised irrigation, including **drip irrigation** and **sprinkler irrigation**.
 
• Drip irrigation is particularly effective for crops like fruits, vegetables, and cash crops, ensuring uniform water distribution.
 
• Localised irrigation reduces water loss due to **evaporation, runoff, and deep percolation**.
 
• It promotes water conservation and enhances **crop productivity**, making it a sustainable irrigation method.
 
• The **Government of India** promotes this method under initiatives such as the **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchai Yojana (PMKSY)** to encourage farmers to adopt efficient irrigation techniques.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Furrow Irrigation**__

 __
 
• **Furrow irrigation** involves creating small parallel channels along the field through which water flows to irrigate crops.
 
• It is a **traditional irrigation method** and is commonly used for crops like maize, sugarcane, and cotton.
 
• This method is less efficient as it can lead to **water wastage** due to evaporation and runoff.
 
 
 
• **Tubewell Irrigation**__
 __
 
• **Tubewell irrigation** involves extracting groundwater using tubewells and pumps.
 
• It is widely used in regions with **ample groundwater availability**, such as Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Though effective, it can lead to the **depletion of groundwater resources** if not managed sustainably.
 
 
 
• **Canal Irrigation**__
 
 
• **Canal irrigation** is a method where water is transported from reservoirs or rivers through canals to agricultural fields.
 
• This method is extensively used in regions like the **Indo-Gangetic plains**.
 
• It requires **large-scale infrastructure** and is suitable for areas with abundant surface water.

 __

• He expanded the Chalukya empire and consolidated its power in the Deccan region.
 
• Kirttivarman I is notable for his patronage of **temple architecture**, continuing the legacy of the Chalukyas in building iconic monuments.
 
 
 
• **Vikramaditya I**__
 __

• He is known for defeating the Pallavas and reasserting Chalukya dominance in South India.
 
• Vikramaditya I contributed significantly to the cultural and architectural advancements of the Chalukyas.

questions.question: Which of the following is a common component in toothpaste, for cleaning the teeth by neutralising the excess acid to prevent tooth decay?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Toothpastes commonly contain **bases like sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) or calcium carbonate**, which help in neutralizing acids in the mouth.
 
• **Acidic substances** in the mouth, often produced by bacterial action on food particles, can lead to **tooth decay**. Bases counteract this acidity to protect teeth.
 
• The base in toothpaste also assists in **removing plaque** and other unwanted residues from the teeth.
 
• **Sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃)** is mildly abrasive, helping in cleaning and polishing the teeth.
 
• Neutralizing the excess acid in the mouth prevents the **erosion of enamel**, which is the protective layer of the teeth.
 
• Additionally, many toothpastes include other ingredients like fluoride for strengthening teeth, but the role of bases is crucial in maintaining the **pH balance** in the oral environment.
 
• By neutralizing acids, bases help in preventing the growth of bacteria that thrive in acidic conditions, thereby promoting better oral hygiene.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Salts**__

 __
 
• **Salts** like sodium chloride or potassium nitrate are sometimes used in toothpaste for specific purposes, such as **reducing tooth sensitivity** or improving taste, but they do not neutralize acids.
 
• Salts primarily act as **additives** and do not play a significant role in the chemical neutralization of acids.
 
 
 
• **Halogens**__
 __
 
• **Halogens** like fluoride (e.g., sodium fluoride) are added to toothpastes for strengthening the teeth and preventing cavities, but they are not bases. They do not neutralize acids.
 
• Fluoride helps in the **remineralization of enamel**, making it more resistant to decay.
 
 
 
• **Acids**__
 
 
• **Acids** are harmful to teeth as they lead to the **degradation of enamel** and promote tooth decay.
 
• Acids are not found in toothpaste because their presence would exacerbate the problem of tooth decay rather than prevent it.

questions.question: Which agreement is linked to the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Assam Accord**__.

__
 
• The **Assam Accord** was signed on **15 August 1985** between the Government of India and leaders of the Assam Movement.
 
• The accord aimed to address the issue of **illegal immigration** into Assam, particularly from neighboring countries like Bangladesh.
 
• The Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985 was introduced as a result of the Assam Accord, amending the Citizenship Act, 1955.
 
• The Assam Accord defined specific cut-off dates for identifying and deporting **illegal immigrants**. People who entered Assam after **March 24, 1971** were to be identified and deported.
 
• The accord also provided for the protection of **Assamese cultural identity**, language, and heritage while addressing the concerns of indigenous communities.
 
• It led to the establishment of mechanisms to detect and deport foreigners, including the formation of **Foreigners' Tribunals**.
 
• The Assam Accord continues to be a cornerstone in debates surrounding **citizenship and immigration policies** in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Shimla Agreement**__

 __
 
• The **Shimla Agreement** was signed on **2 July 1972** between **India and Pakistan** following the Indo-Pak war of 1971.
 
• It aimed at restoring peace and normalizing relations between the two nations.
 
• The agreement established the **Line of Control (LoC)** in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• It holds significance in the context of India's foreign policy and relations with Pakistan but is unrelated to the issue of citizenship or immigration.
 
 
 
• **Indo-Sri Lanka Pact**__
 __
 
• The **Indo-Sri Lanka Pact**, also known as the **Rajiv Gandhi-Jayewardene Accord**, was signed in **1987**.
 
• It aimed at resolving the **Sri Lankan Civil War** and ensuring the rights of Tamil minorities in Sri Lanka.
 
• The pact led to the deployment of the **Indian Peace Keeping Force (IPKF)** in Sri Lanka.
 
• While significant in the context of international relations, it is not connected to the citizenship issues addressed by the Assam Accord.
 
 
 
• **Kashmir Agreement**__
 
 
• The term **Kashmir Agreement** often refers to attempts or discussions to resolve the issue of **Jammu and Kashmir** between India and Pakistan.
 
• It pertains to territorial disputes and regional autonomy rather than citizenship or immigration-related concerns.
 
• It holds importance in the geopolitical context but is unrelated to the Assam Accord or the Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 1985.

questions.question: In the context of file systems, what is the primary purpose of a file system 'metadata'?

options.text: To define the graphical representation of files and folders for the user
To record information about the files and directories, such as their names, sizes, timestamps and permissions
To optimise the physical storage of file data on the storage device for faster access
To store the actual content and data of the files

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**To record information about the files and directories, such as their names, sizes, timestamps, and permissions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **file system metadata** is essential for managing and organizing files and directories on a storage device.
 
• It includes vital information such as the **names, sizes, timestamps (creation, modification, and access times), and permissions** associated with each file and directory.
 
• **Metadata** enables the operating system to locate and access files efficiently, ensuring proper functioning of the file system.
 
• This data is typically stored in specialized structures such as **inodes** (in UNIX-like systems) or **Master File Tables (MFT)** (in NTFS).
 
• It also contains information about the **file structure** (e.g., whether a file is a regular file, directory, or symbolic link).
 
• By maintaining this data, the file system can enforce **security measures** (permissions and access controls) and enable features like **file versioning** or recovery.
 
• Efficient **metadata management** is crucial for system performance, as it directly impacts how quickly files can be located and accessed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **To define the graphical representation of files and folders for the user**__

 __
 
• This option refers to the **user interface** of a file system, which is not the primary function of metadata.
 
• The graphical representation is determined by the **operating system’s file explorer**, such as Windows Explorer or macOS Finder.
 
• While metadata supports file organization, it does not dictate how files and folders appear visually to users.
 
 
 
• **To optimise the physical storage of file data on the storage device for faster access**__
 __
 
• This function falls under **data allocation algorithms** used by the file system to manage physical storage.
 
• Examples include **contiguous allocation, linked allocation, and indexed allocation**.
 
• While metadata can assist in tracking storage blocks, optimization of physical storage is a separate function.
 
 
 
• **To store the actual content and data of the files**__
 
 
• Metadata does not store the **actual file content**; it only describes and tracks the files.
 
• The **actual data** is stored in data blocks or clusters managed by the file system.
 
• Metadata acts as a reference guide, pointing to the location of these data blocks.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is NOT inherently part of a basic 'Blank Presentation' upon its initial creation in MS PowerPoint?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Pre-defined theme colours**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A 'Blank Presentation' in **MS PowerPoint** is designed to provide a completely neutral starting point for users to create their own presentations.
 
• When a blank presentation is created, it includes **at least one slide**, a **default slide layout**, and **placeholders for content** (like titles, subtitles, or text).
 
• However, it does not include **pre-defined theme colours**, which are part of specific templates or themes applied to a presentation.
 
• Theme colours are associated with design templates and help maintain a cohesive and professional appearance in a presentation. These need to be **manually applied** if required.
 
• The absence of pre-defined theme colours allows users to have complete **creative control** over the presentation design, ensuring flexibility for customization.
 
• Users can choose to apply **themes and colour schemes** from the 'Design' tab in PowerPoint if they wish to enhance their slides with a professional layout.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** At least one slide**__

 __
 
• Every new 'Blank Presentation' in PowerPoint includes **at least one slide** by default. This slide often has a **title layout** to help users start their presentation quickly.
 
• The initial slide serves as a placeholder for the presentation title and subtitle.
 
 
 
• ** A default slide layout**__
 __
 
• By default, PowerPoint assigns a **basic slide layout** to the first slide of a blank presentation. This layout typically includes placeholders for text.
 
• Layouts can be changed or customized from the 'Slide Layout' option to match the presentation's needs.
 
 
 
• ** Placeholders for content**__
 
 
• Placeholders are pre-formatted areas on a slide where users can add **text, images, charts, or multimedia**.
 
• In a blank presentation, placeholders for **title and content** are included to simplify the process of creating slides.
 
• Placeholders can be resized, moved, or removed based on the user's requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT contribute much to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Increased plantation of native trees** is a sustainable practice and contributes to the **restoration** of the ecosystem.
 
• Native trees are well-adapted to the **climatic conditions** and soil types of the region, making them ideal for conserving the **local biodiversity.**
 
• Planting native species enhances the ability of the Thar Desert to combat **desertification**, as these trees can provide shade, prevent soil erosion, and improve soil moisture retention.
 
• These trees support the local **wildlife** by providing habitats and food sources, and they also preserve the ecosystem's **natural balance.**
 
• Unlike invasive species, native trees do not disrupt the existing ecological processes. Instead, they contribute to the **stability** and resilience of the environment.
 
• Efforts to plant native trees are often part of **governmental and non-governmental programs** aimed at combating desertification under initiatives such as the **United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD).**
 
• This practice does not lead to any significant degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem but rather helps in its **long-term sustainability.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Grazing by livestock**__

 __
 
• **Grazing by livestock** is a major contributor to the degradation of the Thar Desert ecosystem. Overgrazing leads to **soil erosion** and the destruction of vegetation, which are critical to maintaining the desert’s delicate ecological balance.
 
• Livestock grazing often reduces the availability of **native vegetation**, leading to the loss of habitat for local wildlife.
 
• Excessive grazing also disrupts the soil’s capacity to retain moisture, further exacerbating **desertification.**
 
 
 
• **Erratic rainfall**__
 __
 
• **Erratic rainfall** is another factor impacting the Thar Desert ecosystem. The desert region experiences highly unpredictable and irregular rainfall patterns, which affect the **growth of vegetation** and the availability of water resources.
 
• Sudden bursts of rainfall can lead to **soil erosion**, while prolonged drought periods can decrease the survival rate of plants and animals.
 
• This variability in precipitation is a natural characteristic of desert climates but becomes more pronounced with **climate change.**
 
 
 
• **Climate change**__
 
 
• **Climate change** has a profound impact on the Thar Desert ecosystem, as rising temperatures and changing precipitation patterns intensify **desertification.**
 
• It leads to increased occurrences of **extreme weather events**, such as heatwaves and heavy storms, which disrupt the ecological balance.
 
• Climate change also affects the survival of **native flora and fauna**, as they struggle to adapt to the rapidly changing conditions.
 
• Global efforts to mitigate climate change, such as the **Paris Agreement**, aim to address these challenges to ecosystems worldwide, including the Thar Desert.

questions.question: The Great Plateau of India is a part of which ancient landmass?

__
 
• **Gondwana Land** was a part of the supercontinent **Pangaea**, which existed during the **Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.**
 
• It comprised the present-day landmasses of **South America, Africa, Antarctica, Australia, and the Indian subcontinent.**
 
• The breakup of Gondwana Land led to the formation of the **continents as we know them today.**
 
• The **Great Plateau of India**, which includes the Deccan Plateau, is considered a part of Gondwana Land due to its **geological history and the presence of ancient rocks.**
 
• Gondwana rocks in India contain **coal deposits** and are significant for **mineral extraction**.
 
• The breakup of Gondwana Land is attributed to **tectonic plate movements and continental drift.**
 
• Its name is derived from the **Gondwana region** in India, which was identified as having rocks and fossils from this ancient landmass.
 
• Gondwana Land played a crucial role in the **evolution of life**, with fossils of early plants and animals found in its deposits.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Angaraland**__

 __
 
• **Angaraland** was the northern counterpart of Gondwana Land, forming the other part of the supercontinent **Pangaea**.
 
• It consisted of present-day **Russia, Siberia, and parts of northern Europe.**
 
• Angaraland was separated from Gondwana Land by the **Tethys Sea**, which existed during the Paleozoic and Mesozoic eras.
 
• It played a significant role in the **geological evolution** of the northern hemisphere.
 
 
 
• **Pangaea**__
 __
 
• **Pangaea** was a supercontinent that existed during the **late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic eras.**
 
• It encompassed all of Earth's landmasses before they split into **Laurasia** and **Gondwana Land.**
 
• Pangaea's breakup led to the formation of the continents due to **tectonic plate movements.**
 
• The term "Pangaea" means "all lands" in Greek, highlighting its unified landmass.
 
 
 
• **Laurasia**__
 
 
• **Laurasia** was the northern part of the supercontinent **Pangaea** after its division.
 
• It included the modern landmasses of **North America, Europe, and Asia.**
 
• Laurasia's separation from Gondwana Land marked the **beginning of continental drift.**
 
• It contributed to the formation of the northern hemisphere continents and their geological features.

questions.question: Which of the following measures the percentage of a country's population living below the poverty line?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Poverty Headcount Ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Poverty Headcount Ratio** is a metric used to measure the percentage of a country's population that lives below the **poverty line**.
 
• This indicator helps in understanding the **extent of poverty** in a nation and is widely used in **social and economic analysis**.
 
• It is based on defining a specific **poverty threshold or line**, which represents the minimum income or consumption level required to meet basic needs such as **food, shelter, and clothing**.
 
• The **Poverty Headcount Ratio** is expressed as a percentage of the total population. For example, if 20% of a country's population lives below the poverty line, the ratio is 20%.
 
• This measure is crucial for governments and international organizations like the **World Bank** to assess the impact of their **poverty alleviation programs** and make informed policy decisions.
 
• It is often calculated using data from **household surveys** conducted at national and regional levels.
 
• The indicator is part of broader frameworks like the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**, specifically under Goal 1: No Poverty.
 
• The measure also provides insights into **inequality** and helps target resources toward the most vulnerable groups in society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• ** Gini Coefficient**__

 __
 
• The **Gini Coefficient** is a measure of **income inequality** within a population.
 
• It ranges from **0** (perfect equality) to **1** (maximum inequality).
 
• A lower Gini Coefficient indicates a more **equal income distribution**, whereas a higher value suggests greater inequality.
 
• This metric is often used alongside poverty measures to understand the broader economic disparities in a society.
 
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate**__
 __
 
• The **Unemployment Rate** refers to the percentage of the **labor force** that is unemployed but actively seeking work.
 
• This indicator highlights the **employment situation** in a country but does not directly measure poverty.
 
• It is an important economic metric but does not account for individuals who are **employed but still live in poverty** (working poor).
 
 
 
• **Human Development Index (HDI)**__
 
 
• The **Human Development Index (HDI)** is a composite index that measures a country's overall **social and economic development**.
 
• It considers factors such as **life expectancy, education level, and per capita income**.
 
• Although HDI reflects development levels, it does not specifically measure the **proportion of people living in poverty**.

__
 
• The **Revolt of 1857**, also known as the **First War of Indian Independence**, marked a turning point in the history of British rule in India.
 
• It was a widespread but unsuccessful rebellion against the **British East India Company** rule.
 
• The revolt was triggered due to various factors such as **economic exploitation, political annexation, religious interference, and social injustices**.
 
• One of the key policies that fueled resentment was the **Doctrine of Lapse**, implemented by Lord Dalhousie, which allowed the British to annex Indian princely states if the rulers did not have a direct heir.
 
• The annexation of states like **Awadh** further intensified the discontent among Indian rulers and the local population.
 
• The rebellion was led by figures such as **Rani Lakshmibai of Jhansi, Tantia Tope, Nana Sahib**, and others, who became symbols of resistance.
 
• The revolt demonstrated the widespread dissatisfaction among Indians and revealed the **limitations of the British policies of annexation**.
 
• After suppressing the revolt, the British Crown took direct control of India through the **Government of India Act, 1858**, ending the era of East India Company rule.
 
• The revolt marked the final collapse of the British annexation policy, and subsequent rulers adopted a more cautious approach towards governance and administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 __
 
• The **Partition of Bengal** in 1905 by Lord Curzon was a significant event in Indian history. It divided Bengal into **East Bengal and West Bengal** based on religious and administrative reasons.

• The widespread protests against the partition led to the growth of the **Swadeshi Movement** and ultimately resulted in the reversal of the partition in 1911.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: CD is a volatile storage medium.
ASCII is primarily used for high-speed data transmission networks.
ASCII represents characters as numerical codes.
LAN supports networking over large geographic areas.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**ASCII represents characters as numerical codes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ASCII** stands for **American Standard Code for Information Interchange**, which is a character encoding standard for electronic communication.
 
• It assigns **numerical values** (ranging from 0 to 127) to represent characters such as **letters, digits, punctuation marks, and control characters**.
 
• The use of ASCII allows **computers and electronic devices** to communicate efficiently by representing text in a universally understood manner.
 
• **Each character** (e.g., "A", "B", "1", "!") is mapped to a unique **7-bit binary number**, making it lightweight and efficient for data processing and storage.
 
• It provides a **standardized way of encoding text**, which is essential for compatibility across different systems and applications.
 
• ASCII is widely used in **programming, data processing, and networking**, especially in systems where text representation is critical.
 
• For example, the letter "A" is represented by the **numerical value 65**, and the character "1" is represented by 49 in ASCII.
 
• Extended versions of ASCII (such as **ISO-8859-1**) include additional characters to support other languages and symbols.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **CD is a volatile storage medium**__

 __
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. A **CD (Compact Disc)** is a type of **non-volatile storage medium**, meaning the data stored on it remains intact even when the power is turned off.
 
• CDs are used for storing **audio, video, and data files** and are read using optical drives.
 
• Examples include **CD-ROMs** (read-only memory) and **CD-RWs** (rewritable discs).
 
 
 
• **ASCII is primarily used for high-speed data transmission networks**__
 __
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. ASCII is not designed for high-speed data transmission; it is a **character encoding standard** for representing text.
 
• High-speed data transmission networks use **protocols** like **Ethernet, Fiber Optics, and TCP/IP** for efficient data exchange.
 
 
 
• **LAN supports networking over large geographic areas**__
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**. A **LAN (Local Area Network)** is designed for **small geographic areas**, such as homes, schools, or offices.
 
• Networking over large geographic areas is handled by **WANs (Wide Area Networks)**, such as the Internet.
 
• LANs are known for their **high speed** and **low latency** compared to WANs.
